facts.text: Field recordings used to reconstruct test environments should include accurate poses from the best available GNSS, INS or odometry; in GNSS-denied mines, the state-estimation inputs and solution should be retained.

facts.text: Para-Lane states that RTK/INS trajectories alone are insufficient for aligning frames and adds lidar mapping plus camera-to-lidar registration.

facts.text: Recording virtual-site reconstruction data should include multiple passes and lateral coverage, plus multiple positions, directions and heights for future machines with different sensor heights.
facts.quote: Multiple passes, lateral coverage and, for future machines with different sensor heights, multiple positions, directions and heights.

facts.text: In Para-Lane, training on two lanes and testing between them, called “sandwich,” performed better than extrapolation.
facts.quote: Training on two lanes and testing between them ("sandwich") beat extrapolation in Para-Lane

facts.text: LiDAR-EVS identifies single-traversal training as the source of extrapolation failure.

facts.text: In XLD, three cameras substantially reduced the reported drop compared with one camera.
facts.quote: Multiple cameras: in XLD three cameras reduced the drop substantially compared with one.

facts.text: COLMAP recommends good texture, similar illumination, high overlap, at least three observations per object and genuinely different camera positions for reconstruction.
facts.quote: COLMAP recommends good texture, similar illumination, high overlap, at least three observations per object and genuinely different camera positions

facts.text: COLMAP warns that pure camera rotation is inadequate for reconstruction.
facts.quote: warns that pure rotation is inadequate

facts.text: COLMAP notes that many near-identical frames do not replace different viewpoints and suggests downsampling video.
facts.quote: notes that many near-identical frames do not replace viewpoints (it suggests downsampling video).

facts.text: Mapping runs should use clear weather; Para-Lane selected clear sunny days with uncongested road conditions.
facts.quote: Clear weather for the mapping run: Para-Lane selected "clear sunny days with uncongested road conditions".

facts.text: Lidar recordings for environment reconstruction should retain the rawest useful representation, including timestamps, point positions, return and intensity, and sensor configuration, rather than a decimated visualisation cloud.
facts.quote: The rawest useful lidar representation (timestamps, point positions, return and intensity, sensor configuration) rather than a decimated visualisation cloud

facts.text: Radar recordings for environment reconstruction should retain richer detections or raw or intermediate measurements rather than a final tracked-object list, because the final list has already discarded most environment information.
facts.quote: for radar, richer detections or raw or intermediate measurements rather than a final tracked-object list, which has already discarded most of the environment information.

facts.text: Incorrect sensor transforms or timestamps can make several accurate sensors produce an inaccurate reconstructed scene.
facts.quote: Poor calibration or synchronisation: several accurate sensors build an inaccurate scene if their transforms or timestamps are wrong.

facts.text: ECU-GS documented calibration drift from vibration on rough off-road terrain in 2026.
facts.quote: Calibration drift from vibration on rough terrain is documented off-road (ECU-GS, 2026).

facts.text: Only 50 of 200 recorded MV² scenes met the training-set pose-quality threshold of maximum epipolar error below 30.
facts.quote: Pose failures: only 50 of 200 recorded MV² scenes satisfied the training-set threshold (maximum epipolar error below 30).

facts.text: Single forward-facing passes and insufficient parallax or coverage can cause environment reconstruction to fail.
facts.quote: Single forward-facing passes and insufficient parallax or coverage.

facts.text: Textureless or repetitive terrain, including uniform soil, snow, tunnel walls and crop rows, weakens visual correspondence during reconstruction.
facts.quote: Textureless or repetitive terrain: uniform soil, snow, tunnel walls or crop rows weaken visual correspondence

facts.text: Lidar or surveyed control is especially valuable for reconstruction of textureless or repetitive terrain that weakens visual correspondence.
facts.quote: uniform soil, snow, tunnel walls or crop rows weaken visual correspondence, which makes lidar or surveyed control especially valuable.

facts.text: Moving objects and dynamic-mask errors can cause workers, machines, swinging booms and vegetation to be reconstructed at incompatible positions unless the static background is separated from dynamic tracks.
facts.quote: Moving objects, including dynamic-mask errors: workers, machines, swinging booms and vegetation are reconstructed at incompatible positions unless the static background is separated from dynamic tracks.

facts.text: Ground4D identifies fine-detail terrain, ego-motion jitter and moving vegetation as reconstruction failure factors in May 2026.
facts.quote: Fine-detail terrain, ego-motion jitter and moving vegetation (Ground4D, May 2026).

facts.text: EUVS identifies lighting changes between passes as a reconstruction failure factor, based on on-road evidence.
facts.quote: Lighting changes between passes (EUVS)

facts.text: Strong glare, shadow and reflective surfaces are reconstruction failure factors; COLMAP warns against high dynamic range and specularities.
facts.quote: strong glare, shadow and reflective surfaces (COLMAP warns against high dynamic range and specularities).

facts.text: MV² identifies large height changes as a reconstruction failure factor, based on on-road evidence.
facts.quote: Large height changes (MV²).

facts.text: Dust, snow, rain and fog are desirable test phenomena but undesirable mapping observations because transient returns and obscuration become mixed into the supposedly permanent site model.
facts.quote: Dust, snow, rain and fog in the recordings: desirable test phenomena but undesirable mapping observations, because transient returns and obscuration become mixed into the supposedly permanent site model.

facts.text: A workable separation of mapping and adverse-weather testing preserves the raw adverse-weather run for sensor replay and reconstructs the static site from cleaner data.
facts.quote: A workable split preserves the raw adverse-weather run for sensor replay and reconstructs the static site from cleaner data.

facts.text: No off-road study was found quantifying the problem of adverse-weather recordings mixing transient returns and obscuration into a permanent reconstructed site model.
facts.quote: No off-road study quantifying this was found.

facts.text: A route-mounted sensor cannot recover surfaces that the sensor never observed.
facts.quote: Occlusion: a route-mounted sensor cannot recover surfaces it never saw

facts.text: Neural synthesis can visually fill unobserved surfaces, but generated content should not silently become geometric truth in a reconstructed environment.
facts.quote: neural synthesis can fill them visually, but generated content should not silently become geometric truth.

facts.text: RGB footage cannot provide a simulator with the radar or acoustic properties of a surface.
facts.quote: Missing material truth: RGB footage cannot tell the simulator the radar or acoustic properties of a surface.

facts.text: The proposed conversion pipeline from field recordings to test environments is expert opinion assembled from cited reconstruction, geospatial and simulation sources, not a published standard.
